## Verdict: the finding is there — the repo ships no agent surface at all

`crimes_00011` — **Missing Agent Context**, medium severity, confidence 0.9, `agent_risk` 0.47:

```
type:        missing_agent_context
detector_id: missing_agent_context   (pack: universal)
evidence:    no AGENTS.md found at repo root
             no CLAUDE.md found at repo root
             no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present
             no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present
             package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands
effort:      small
```

One caveat on reading it: the finding is anchored to `assets/cjs_shims.js`, but it's a **repo-level** finding, not a problem with that file — the detector just needs somewhere to hang. Don't go looking for a crime in the shims.

## What that costs you on your first PR

The scan hands you the specifics of what an agent would get wrong here, and they're all things a paragraph of prose would have prevented:

- **It won't know how to build or test.** `package.json` exposes `tsup` and `tsup-node` binaries, but nothing tells an agent which script runs the suite, whether the tests need a prior build, or that `test/` is integration-heavy (tests shell out and inspect build output via `test/utils.ts`). An agent will guess `npm test` and either wedge or silently skip the real check.
- **It'll refactor load-bearing files casually.** `src/utils.ts` (fan-in 18, 425 lines), `src/plugin.ts` (fan-in 10), `src/log.ts` (fan-in 9), `test/utils.ts` (fan-in 9). Nothing marks these as high-blast-radius, so a "tidy up" pass in `utils.ts` ripples through 29 importers.
- **The test suite gives false confidence.** 12 tests with **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls (`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`, `test/tsconfig.test.ts`, `test/experimental-dts.test.ts`) plus 13 more with only weak matchers. Green CI does not mean your change is safe, and an agent has no way to know that.
- **It'll trip the naming traps.** `build()`, `buildAll()`, `buildStart()` and `getRollupConfig()` all read as pure but perform side effects (`removeFiles`, `createLogger`, `setSilent`) — four separate False Identity findings. An agent that treats `getRollupConfig` as a read will delete files.

Net effect: confident, plausible-looking edits that pass a suite which proves nothing.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

Root-level `AGENTS.md`. The detector accepts any one of AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / a SKILL.md, so this single file is enough. Fill the `<>` placeholders from the real `package.json` scripts — everything else below is drawn straight from the scan.

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Bundler for TypeScript/JavaScript libraries (esbuild + rollup for dts).
Read this before editing.

## Commands

- Install: `<pnpm install>`
- Build: `<pnpm build>`
- Test: `<pnpm test>` — integration-heavy; most tests run a real build
  into a temp dir and assert on the output. Slow. Build first.
- Typecheck: `<pnpm typecheck>`
- Single test: `<pnpm test -- -t "test name">`

## Layout

- `src/index.ts` — public entry, `build()` orchestration and option normalization
- `src/esbuild/` — esbuild pipeline and per-loader plugins (svelte, swc, postcss)
- `src/rollup.ts`, `src/api-extractor.ts`, `src/tsc.ts` — `.d.ts` generation
- `src/plugin.ts` — plugin container / lifecycle hooks
- `test/` — integration tests; `test/utils.ts` is the shared harness

## Load-bearing files — prefer additive changes

Do not restructure these without being asked:

- `src/utils.ts` — 18 importers
- `src/plugin.ts` — 10 importers
- `src/log.ts` — 9 importers
- `test/utils.ts` — 9 importers (every test file depends on its shape)

## Conventions and traps

- **`build*` and `get*` are not pure.** `build()`, `buildAll()`,
  `buildStart()` and `getRollupConfig()` delete files, mutate logger
  state, and write to disk. Read the body before assuming a call is safe.
- Sync I/O is intentional in `src/utils.ts` and `src/fs.ts` (CLI startup
  path). Don't convert to async as drive-by cleanup.
- Options flow as one wide `options` bag through `normalizeOptions` →
  `runEsbuild` → plugins. Add new options at the entry point, not midway.

## Before you open a PR

- Run the build and the test suite.
- **A green suite is weaker than it looks:** several tests assert
  nothing at all (`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`,
  `test/shims.test.ts`). If you touch behaviour they nominally cover,
  add a real assertion rather than trusting the pass.
- Add a test that fails without your change.
```

## Cost and verification

`effort: small` — this is a one-file, ~50-line PR, and it's a good thing to land *first* so the rest of your work benefits from it. Confirm it cleared:

```bash
crimes scan --format json | jq '.findings[] | select(.type == "missing_agent_context")'
```

Empty output means the charge is dropped. It won't move the other 86 findings — `agent_risk` on `utils.ts` and the God Functions stays where it is — but it converts "the agent has to infer everything" into "the agent was told," which is the cheapest risk reduction available in this repo.
